en: to dart one's tongue in and out

examples.en: That snake over there keeps flicking its tongue.

examples.ko: 강아지가 물을 마실 때 혀를 날름거리면서 마셔요.
examples.en: The puppy laps up water, flicking its tongue.
It was fascinating to watch the lizard flick its tongue.
Flames flickered inside the stove.
Don't flick your tongue around; eat politely.
The child flicked out his tongue at the sight of the ice cream.

explain: 혀나 불길이 자꾸 빠르게 나왔다 들어갔다 하는 모습에 써요. '날름대다'와 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: Use it when a tongue or flame keeps darting in and out quickly. It can be swapped with '날름대다' with the same meaning.

examples.en: When spring comes, pussy willows bloom by the brook.
When I touched the pussy willow, it was soft like down.
The children played holding pussy willow twigs they had snapped off.
The fluffy pussy willow is really cute.

examples.ko: 이른 봄에 버들강아지를 보면 기분이 좋아져요.
examples.en: Seeing pussy willows in early spring makes me feel good.
The pussy willow in the photo sparkles in the sunlight.

explain: 진짜 강아지가 아니라 이른 봄에 버드나무 종류에 피는 솜털 같은 꽃이삭이에요. 봄이 오는 것을 알리는 모습으로 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Despite the name, it is not a puppy but the fuzzy, downy flower spike that appears on willow trees in early spring. It fits well when talking about the arrival of spring.

examples.en: There is a crater at the top of Hallasan.
Water collected in the crater and became a lake.
I want to see a volcano's crater up close.
It is dangerous to go inside the crater.
There is a big lake in the crater of Baekdusan.
Smoke rose from the crater.

explain: 화산 분화구에 물이 고이면 '화구호'라고 해요. 백두산 천지가 가장 유명한 예예요. 달 표면의 둥근 구덩이는 '크레이터'라는 말을 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: When water collects in a volcanic crater it is called a 화구호 (crater lake), and Baekdusan's 천지 is the best-known example. For the round pits on the moon, the word 크레이터 is used more often.

examples.en: I got bitten by red ants in the mountains and it hurt a lot.

examples.ko: 불개미가 집 앞 화단에 줄지어 다녀요.
examples.en: Red ants are walking in a line in the flower bed in front of my house.

examples.ko: 불개미는 나무 밑에 집을 짓고 살아요.
examples.en: Red ants build nests under trees and live there.
If a red ant bites you, it stings and swells.
I was startled to see a swarm of red ants.
I sprayed insecticide to get rid of the red ants.

explain: 붉은빛이 나는 개미를 말하고, 물리면 따끔해서 조심하라는 이야기에 자주 나와요. 뉴스에서는 외국에서 들어온 '붉은불개미'라는 이름으로 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It refers to reddish ants, and comes up often when people warn that their bite stings. In the news it often appears under the name '붉은불개미' for the red imported fire ant.

examples.en: The cat batted the toy with its front paw.
The puppy raises its front paw to say hello.
The horse raised its front legs and neighed loudly.
I went to the clinic to treat the injured front paw.
The bear caught a fish with its front paw.
Our dog scratches the door with its front paw.

explain: 짝말은 '뒷발'이에요. 동물에게는 '손' 대신 '앞발'을 쓰고, 다리 전체를 말할 때는 '앞다리'라고 해요. 개나 고양이가 앞발로 무엇을 하는지 말할 때 '앞발로 ~하다'가 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The paired word is '뒷발' (hind paw). For animals you say '앞발' instead of '손', and '앞다리' for the whole front leg. The pattern '앞발로 ~하다' often describes what a dog or cat does with its front paw.

en: to come and go; to move back and forth

examples.ko: 요즘 날씨가 오락가락해서 옷 입기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: The weather keeps changing these days, so it's hard to decide what to wear.
It's raining on and off, so take an umbrella.

examples.ko: 오락가락하는 태도 때문에 그 사람을 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to trust that person because of the way they keep changing their attitude.
The fever was so high that I kept drifting in and out of consciousness.
The patient keeps drifting in and out of consciousness.
The stock price fluctuated and finally went down.

explain: 비, 날씨, 기분, 정신처럼 왔다 갔다 하며 일정하지 않은 것에 써요. 단순히 오가는 동작은 '왔다 갔다 하다'라고 더 일상적으로 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for things that go back and forth without staying steady, such as rain, weather, mood or consciousness. For simply moving back and forth, the more everyday expression is '왔다 갔다 하다'.

examples.en: I got a lacquer rash, and my whole body itches.
My arms turned red, maybe from a lacquer rash I got in the mountains.

examples.ko: 옻 때문에 병원에 가야 할 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think I have to go to the hospital because of the lacquer.
I'm sensitive to lacquer, so I'm careful.

examples.ko: 옻이 올랐을 때는 긁지 말고 병원에 가세요.
examples.en: When you get a lacquer rash, don't scratch it, go to the doctor.

examples.ko: 옻으로 칠한 그릇은 오래 써도 윤이 나요.
examples.en: Bowls painted with lacquer stay shiny even after long use.

explain: '옻이 오르다', '옻을 타다'가 가장 흔한 표현이에요. 옻나무를 만지거나 옻으로 만든 음식을 먹고 피부가 가려워질 때 말해요.
explain_en: The most common expressions are '옻이 오르다' and '옻을 타다'. They are used when your skin gets itchy after touching lacquer trees or eating food made with them.

examples.en: When spring came, buds sprouted on every branch.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 비가 내리면 씨앗이 움트기 시작해요.
examples.en: When warm rain falls, the seeds start to sprout.

examples.ko: 두 사람 사이에 사랑이 움트는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems love is budding between the two of them.

examples.ko: 제 꿈이 움튼 곳이 바로 이 동네예요.
examples.en: This very neighborhood is where my dream first took root.

examples.ko: 이 마을에서 새로운 희망이 움트고 있어요.
examples.en: New hope is springing up in this village.
When winter ends, grass seeds also sprout underground.

explain: 식물의 싹이 나오는 일에 쓰고, 사랑·희망·생각이 처음 생겨나는 것에도 많이 써요. 비슷한 말로 '싹트다'가 있어요. 활용은 '움트다 - 움터요 - 움텄어요'예요.
explain_en: It is used for plant buds coming out, and often for love, hope or ideas starting to form. '싹트다' is a similar word. The conjugation goes '움트다 - 움터요 - 움텄어요'.

en: to be steep; to be rugged; to be forbidding

examples.ko: 이 지역은 산이 험준해서 길을 내기 어려워요.
examples.en: The mountains here are rugged, so it's hard to build roads.

examples.ko: 험준한 산맥을 넘어 옆 나라로 갔어요.
examples.en: We crossed the rugged mountain range into the next country.
The terrain is rugged, so be careful when hiking.

examples.ko: 험준한 바위 길이라서 장비가 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: It's a steep, rocky path, so you definitely need gear.

examples.ko: 산이 험준해서 눈이 오면 아무도 올라가지 못해요.
examples.en: The mountain is so rugged that nobody can climb it when it snows.
It's a mountain famous for being rugged, so it's hard for beginners.

explain: 산, 지형, 길이 가파르고 거칠어서 다니기 힘들다고 할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '험하다'를 더 자주 쓰고, '험준하다'는 설명하는 글이나 뉴스, 여행 소개에서 잘 보여요. '험준한 산', '험준한 지형'처럼 함께 써요.
explain_en: It describes mountains, terrain or paths that are steep and rough to travel. In daily talk people use '험하다' more, while '험준하다' shows up in descriptions, news and travel guides. Typical pairings are '험준한 산' and '험준한 지형'.

examples.en: I saw a bull for the first time in a country village.
A bull is really strong.
My grandfather plowed the field with an ox.
That bull suddenly ran toward us and I was startled.

examples.ko: 황소만큼 큰 개를 키우는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Someone keeps a dog as big as an ox.

examples.ko: 동상 앞에 황소 두 마리가 서 있어요.
examples.en: Two bulls are standing in front of the statue.

explain: 그냥 '소'라고 하면 암컷과 수컷 모두예요. '황소'는 크고 힘센 수컷 소, 특히 농사일을 하던 소를 말해요. 암소는 '암소', 어린 소는 '송아지'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 아버지는 황소고집이라서 한번 정하면 안 바꿔요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한번 마음먹으면 절대 안 바꾸는 아주 센 고집을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes extreme stubbornness; someone who never changes their mind once it is made up.

explain_en: 소 on its own covers cows and bulls alike; 황소 is the big, powerful male, especially the kind used for farm work. A female is 암소 and a calf is 송아지.
